claims.text: The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is not satisfied on this record. The call limb is met — one in-app call at 11:14:20, unanswered, ringing 20 s — but the message limb is not: no in-app chat message from the driver appears anywhere before the 11:18:10 cancellation. The only entry on file is the rider's own 11:06:00 message, and the chat export is IMPAIRED — issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6 — because only 1 of the 3 entries that trip_record.chat_message_count reports was exported and nothing after 11:06:00 survives, so the arrival and the entire waiting window are unrecorded. The derived contact_before_cancel block records message_count 0 and obligation_met false. POL-NS-23 voids the fee where either limb is missing, so the 5.00 SGD must not be charged to the rider.

If the truncated export is treated as leaving it open whether the driver ever messaged the rider, that is precisely the situation POL-GEN-26 covers: whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling is a fact POL-NS-23 needs and cannot be established from this record, because the evidence that would carry it is impaired — EV-CHAT-05065, TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6. POL-GEN-26 directs that the case be escalated with the open question stated and that no outcome be inferred from the absence of evidence. An escalated fee is held rather than collected, so on this route the rider still does not carry the disputed charge.

The dispute was filed by the DRIVER (dispute.filed_by = DRIVER), not by the rider, and the payments ledger already shows the fee reversed: payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00, the 5.00 SGD withheld from the driver pending this review (EV-FARE-05065). Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling values are party-relative — FULL_REFUND means the FILING party is entirely right — so on a driver-filed no-show a FULL_REFUND finding would run for the driver and against the rider. What leaves the rider not carrying the charge is NO_ACTION: the filing driver's claim is not supported and the present refunded state stands. The rider asks for that; failing it, for the POL-GEN-26 escalation in the preceding claim, which holds the amount.

Nothing in the record supports the driver's assertion that the rider 'never came out'. The rider's own 11:06:00 message reads 'Hi, I'm at the Blk 19 lobby, will come out when you reach', which places the rider at the pickup and shows an intention to board — and the chat log it sits in is impaired (EV-CHAT-05065, TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6), so it is relied on only for that single retained entry. Critically, the trace carries no rider track at all: rider_track is empty, so no location evidence in this case puts the rider anywhere but the lobby they said they were at. POL-GEN-26 forbids reading a no-show outcome out of the mere absence of evidence.

claims.text: The driver was at the pickup at 11:11:50. The trip record's auto-arrival event is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace — 25 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s — whose nearest fix sits 2.05 m from the pickup point with 5 m reported accuracy, inside both the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter. The trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the arrival limb of POL-NS-21 rests on clean evidence.

The free wait was served in full before any cancellation. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled pickup time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 11:11:50 and expired at 11:16:50; the driver cancelled at 11:18:10, 380 s after arrival and 80 s past the end of the free wait. The cancellation was therefore taken after the free wait, exactly as POL-NS-21 requires.

The fee is exactly the policy fee and the money mechanism is clean. The payments ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD against a policy fee of 5.00 SGD, with fee_matches_policy true and no distance, time, surge or platform component. Under POL-NS-22 the whole fee passes to the driver (fee_share_to_driver 1.00) and the derived money block gives driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd of 5.00. The interim reversal that refunded the rider and withheld the 5.00 from the driver should be undone, and the ruling entered as DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to 5.00.

The call limb of the driver's contact obligation is on the record. One in-app call was placed by the driver at 11:14:20, ringing 20 s unanswered, and it was placed before trip_record.cancelled_at of 11:18:10 — which is precisely what POL-NS-23 requires of the call, and precisely the source POL-NS-23 names for it (trip_record.in_app_calls).

The message limb cannot be decided against the driver on this record. The only artifact bearing on it is IMPAIRED: the chat log fires TRUNCATED_LOG and carries weight 0.6, because it exports 1 of the trip record's 3 chat messages and holds nothing after 11:06:00, covering neither the arrival nor the waiting window. A 0.6 artifact cannot carry the negative finding that no message was sent, and under POL-GEN-02 that impairment must be disclosed, names TRUNCATED_LOG, and caps any finding drawn from it. The record therefore does not establish that the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 failed; at most it leaves the point open.

The rider knew the driver was there and did not come out. The platform pushed 'Your driver has arrived' to her at 11:11:54, and the single chat entry the impaired log does hold (TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6) is her own message at 11:06:00 saying she was at the Blk 19 lobby and would come out when he reached. She had still not appeared and had not answered the 20 s call when the free wait expired at 11:16:50. The 5.00 SGD is compensation for the driver's time and fuel under POL-NS-22, and on those facts it was earned.

POL-NS-24 has no application here. That clause lets the rider cancel at no charge where the driver missed the pickup by the scheduled time plus 5 minutes, with a goodwill credit if contact was also not attempted. The record carries no scheduled pickup time at all, the driver did arrive and did wait, and the rider never cancelled — the trip was cancelled by the driver for rider no-show. The deadline POL-NS-24 needs is only needed if the rider cancelled, and she did not, so the rider's free-cancellation route is closed and no goodwill credit is owed.

If the panel treats the message limb as unestablished rather than met, POL-GEN-26 governs and still does not give the rider the money. 'Whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling' is one of the facts POL-GEN-26 names by name, and the remedy it prescribes is escalation with the amount held rather than returned. ESCALATE is therefore the correct floor for the driver on this record: the 5.00 SGD stays held pending human review instead of being confirmed back to the rider.

No other threshold opens a human-review path, so the merits here can be decided. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD line, so under POL-GEN-22 the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries fraud_flags (both 0, so the 0.95 bar is not engaged); no safety indicator appears in the record; and POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final subject only to those bars and to POL-GEN-26. The only escalation question on this record is the message limb, addressed above — and on the merits the driver's fee stands.

ruling.explanation:
Driver D-80283 and Rider R-78865: this case goes to human review, and the 5.00 SGD stays held rather than confirmed to either side. Here is why.

What is established. The driver arrived at the pickup at 11:11:50, and the trip record's auto-arrival is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace: the nearest fix sits 2.05 m from the pickup point with 5 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter (POL-NS-21). The trip was on-demand with no scheduled time, so the 300-second free wait ran from arrival and expired at 11:16:50; the driver cancelled at 11:18:10, 80 seconds past the wait (POL-NS-21). The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee with no other component (POL-NS-22).

What is not established, and why it decides the case. POL-NS-23 requires the driver to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call before cancelling. The call limb is met: one in-app call at 11:14:20, unanswered, ringing 20 seconds, before the 11:18:10 cancellation. The message limb is undecided. The only chat artifact, EV-CHAT-05065, is impaired — truncated, issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6 — exporting 1 of the 3 messages the trip record reports and holding nothing after 11:06:00. The arrival and the entire waiting window, exactly when a message would have been sent, are unrecorded; the one retained entry is the rider's own 11:06:00 message. Whether the driver messaged before cancelling is a fact POL-NS-23 needs and this record cannot supply, because the evidence that would carry it is impaired. POL-GEN-26 therefore applies and sends the case to human review; no outcome is inferred from the missing evidence.

On the competing claims. The driver's request that the fee be confirmed as DRIVER_COMPENSATION is not granted: the contact obligation is undecided, so the fee cannot be confirmed. The rider's request for FULL_REFUND under POL-NS-23 is not granted either: an impaired log cannot establish that no message was sent any more than it can establish that one was. The rider's alternative that NO_ACTION simply leaves the reversal in place is not adopted, because an undecided limb supports neither the payment nor the refund — the amount is held. Nothing turns on the empty rider_track: it does not establish that the rider boarded, and it does not void the fee. POL-NS-24 has no application — there was no scheduled pickup time and the rider never cancelled.

Thresholds, confidence and referrals. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line (AI final at any confidence), and neither profile carries a fraud flag (both 0). POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final subject to POL-GEN-26, which is the provision that escalates here. Confidence is 0.6, capped by the impaired chat log (TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6) that carries the undecided fact. No referral is produced: the fee is exactly 5.00 SGD (POL-NS-22's referral fires only on a different amount), no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit is due, and the rider's profile does not carry the POL-NS-25 repeat no-show counter.

Open question for the reviewer: did D-80283 send an in-app chat message to R-78865 before the 11:18:10 cancellation? The truncated chat export must be recovered or the point otherwise resolved. If no message was sent, the 5.00 SGD fee is void and the refund to the rider stands; if one was sent, the fee stands and the 5.00 SGD is due to the driver.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this case turns on one fact the record cannot settle, so the 5.00 SGD fee is held for human review rather than confirmed to the driver or returned to the rider.

What is established. The driver reached the pickup at 11:11:50 — the trip record's auto-arrival is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest fix sits 2.05 m from the pickup with 5 m reported accuracy, well inside the 50 m STANDARD radius and the 25 m accuracy filter (EV-GPS-05065, COMPLETE, weight 1.0). The trip was on demand with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from arrival and expired at 11:16:50; the driver cancelled at 11:18:10, 380 seconds after arrival and 80 seconds past the end of the wait. The driver also placed one in-app call at 11:14:20, unanswered after 20 seconds, before cancelling — the call half of POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met.

What cannot be established. POL-NS-23 also requires at least one in-app chat message from the driver before cancelling, and it voids the fee if either half is missing. The only artifact that could show that message is the chat log, and it is impaired — issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6 (EV-CHAT-05065): 1 of the 3 messages the trip record reports was exported, and nothing after 11:06:00 survives, so the arrival and the entire waiting window are unrecorded. The log therefore cannot carry a finding that no message was sent, and equally cannot carry one that a message was sent. The rider's statement that she received no message does not settle it: POL-NS-23 tests whether the driver sent a message, not whether it was received, and a counterparty statement is not the artifact that clause names. The message limb is therefore undecided, and an undecided limb supports neither the fee (which needs the obligation met) nor a refund (which needs it failed). POL-GEN-26 governs exactly this situation — whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling is a fact POL-NS-23 needs and cannot be established from impaired evidence — and directs escalation with the open question stated.

Consequences for each side's ask. The driver's request for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD cannot be granted, because POL-NS-22 pays only where the POL-NS-23 contact obligation is met and the message half is undecided. The rider's request that the fee be voided under POL-NS-23 likewise cannot be granted, because the impaired log cannot establish that a message was missing. The rider's fallback — that a driver-filed case should be resolved as NO_ACTION so the already-refunded state stands — is not available either: POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION the finding that the filing party's claim is not supported, which would require deciding the message limb against the driver, and it is undecided.

The remaining clauses add nothing. POL-NS-24 does not apply (the rider never cancelled, and no scheduled time exists to fix its deadline, so no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arises). POL-NS-22's fee-amount check is satisfied (EV-FARE-05065 charged exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so no referral). POL-NS-25 does not fire (the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter, and the rule applies only when that field is present). No safety indicator appears in the record, and neither profile carries a fraud flag.

Review and confidence. The dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 set no confidence bar to a no-show decision; the escalation rests on POL-GEN-26's missing fact, not on confidence. Because the ruling rests on the impaired chat log (weight 0.6), confidence is capped at 0.6. The 5.00 SGD is held: it is neither confirmed to the driver nor returned to the rider. The open question for the reviewer is whether the driver sent an in-app chat message to the rider before cancelling; the full chat export (3 entries) should be obtained.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: I am escalating this case to a human reviewer under POL-GEN-26, and the disputed 5.00 SGD stays held — neither confirmed to the driver nor returned to the rider — until that review is done.

What the record settles cleanly. The driver's arrival is proved: EV-TRIP-05065 (weight 1.0) records the auto-arrival at 11:11:50, and EV-GPS-05065 (weight 1.0) corroborates it with a nearest fix 2.05 m from the pickup point at 5 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s (5-minute) free wait ran from that arrival and expired at 11:16:50; the driver cancelled at 11:18:10, after the wait. That limb is met. The fee is exactly the policy figure: EV-FARE-05065 (weight 1.0) shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line against the 5.00 SGD policy fee, fee_matches_policy true, so POL-NS-22's amount check does not fire.

What the record cannot settle. POL-NS-23 voids the fee unless the driver both sent at least one in-app chat message and placed at least one in-app call before cancelling. The call limb is met — one in-app call at 11:14:20, unanswered, before the 11:18:10 cancellation (trip record, the source POL-NS-23 names). The message limb is not. EV-CHAT-05065 is IMPAIRED (issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6): it exports only 1 of the 3 chat messages the trip record reports and holds nothing after 11:06:00, so it covers neither the arrival nor the whole waiting window. Whether the driver messaged the rider is therefore a fact POL-NS-23 needs and this record cannot establish either way. POL-GEN-26 names that very fact ('whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling') and directs escalation with the open question stated, and POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final only subject to POL-GEN-26. An undecided limb supports neither a payment that needs the clause to hold nor a refund that needs it to fail, so the fee can be neither confirmed nor voided on this record.

The claims. The rider's POL-NS-23/FULL_REFUND theory is rejected: the impaired log does not establish that a driver message is missing, and no outcome may be inferred from its absence (POL-GEN-26). The rider's POL-GEN-26 escalation claim is accepted, and it is what decides the case. The rider's POL-GEN-03 party-relative NO_ACTION request is not reached, because an escalation replaces any money outcome. The rider's point that rider_track is empty is noted but does not help: this is the driver-device trace, and the absence of a rider-side track is not evidence the rider was absent. The driver's DRIVER_COMPENSATION request is outweighed by the undecided message limb; his own point that the message limb cannot be decided against him is accepted, and it is exactly why the fee is not voided. The driver's POL-NS-24 point is accepted — no scheduled time, driver arrived, rider never cancelled, so no free-cancellation route and no goodwill credit. On thresholds (POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26): the 5.00 SGD contested is below the 10.00 SGD line, neither profile carries fraud_flags, and no safety indicator appears, so the AI could be final — but POL-NS-26 is expressly subject to POL-GEN-26, which requires escalation here.

Referrals. None: POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not apply, POL-NS-25 does not fire (the rider's counter is below 3), and POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire (the fee is exactly 5.00 SGD).

Open question for the reviewer: did the driver send an in-app chat message to the rider before cancelling at 11:18:10? The truncated chat export cannot answer it.

Confidence: 0.6, capped by EV-CHAT-05065 (weight 0.6, issue code TRUNCATED_LOG), the impaired artifact this escalation rests on. The interim reversal already refunded the rider and withheld the 5.00 SGD from the driver; on this ruling the amount remains held pending human review.

ledger.claim: The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is not satisfied on this record. The call limb is met — one in-app call at 11:14:20, unanswered, ringing 20 s — but the message limb is not: no in-app chat message from the driver appears anywhere before the 11:18:10 cancellation. The only entry on file is the rider's own 11:06:00 message, and the chat export is IMPAIRED — issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6 — because only 1 of the 3 entries that trip_record.chat_message_count reports was exported and nothing after 11:06:00 survives, so the arrival and the entire waiting window are unrecorded. The derived contact_before_cancel block records message_count 0 and obligation_met false. POL-NS-23 voids the fee where either limb is missing, so the 5.00 SGD must not be charged to the rider.

If the truncated export is treated as leaving it open whether the driver ever messaged the rider, that is precisely the situation POL-GEN-26 covers: whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling is a fact POL-NS-23 needs and cannot be established from this record, because the evidence that would carry it is impaired — EV-CHAT-05065, TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6. POL-GEN-26 directs that the case be escalated with the open question stated and that no outcome be inferred from the absence of evidence. An escalated fee is held rather than collected, so on this route the rider still does not carry the disputed charge.

The dispute was filed by the DRIVER (dispute.filed_by = DRIVER), not by the rider, and the payments ledger already shows the fee reversed: payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00, the 5.00 SGD withheld from the driver pending this review (EV-FARE-05065). Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling values are party-relative — FULL_REFUND means the FILING party is entirely right — so on a driver-filed no-show a FULL_REFUND finding would run for the driver and against the rider. What leaves the rider not carrying the charge is NO_ACTION: the filing driver's claim is not supported and the present refunded state stands. The rider asks for that; failing it, for the POL-GEN-26 escalation in the preceding claim, which holds the amount.

Nothing in the record supports the driver's assertion that the rider 'never came out'. The rider's own 11:06:00 message reads 'Hi, I'm at the Blk 19 lobby, will come out when you reach', which places the rider at the pickup and shows an intention to board — and the chat log it sits in is impaired (EV-CHAT-05065, TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6), so it is relied on only for that single retained entry. Critically, the trace carries no rider track at all: rider_track is empty, so no location evidence in this case puts the rider anywhere but the lobby they said they were at. POL-GEN-26 forbids reading a no-show outcome out of the mere absence of evidence.

The driver was at the pickup at 11:11:50. The trip record's auto-arrival event is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace — 25 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s — whose nearest fix sits 2.05 m from the pickup point with 5 m reported accuracy, inside both the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter. The trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the arrival limb of POL-NS-21 rests on clean evidence.

The free wait was served in full before any cancellation. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled pickup time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 11:11:50 and expired at 11:16:50; the driver cancelled at 11:18:10, 380 s after arrival and 80 s past the end of the free wait. The cancellation was therefore taken after the free wait, exactly as POL-NS-21 requires.

The fee is exactly the policy fee and the money mechanism is clean. The payments ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD against a policy fee of 5.00 SGD, with fee_matches_policy true and no distance, time, surge or platform component. Under POL-NS-22 the whole fee passes to the driver (fee_share_to_driver 1.00) and the derived money block gives driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd of 5.00. The interim reversal that refunded the rider and withheld the 5.00 from the driver should be undone, and the ruling entered as DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to 5.00.

The call limb of the driver's contact obligation is on the record. One in-app call was placed by the driver at 11:14:20, ringing 20 s unanswered, and it was placed before trip_record.cancelled_at of 11:18:10 — which is precisely what POL-NS-23 requires of the call, and precisely the source POL-NS-23 names for it (trip_record.in_app_calls).

The message limb cannot be decided against the driver on this record. The only artifact bearing on it is IMPAIRED: the chat log fires TRUNCATED_LOG and carries weight 0.6, because it exports 1 of the trip record's 3 chat messages and holds nothing after 11:06:00, covering neither the arrival nor the waiting window. A 0.6 artifact cannot carry the negative finding that no message was sent, and under POL-GEN-02 that impairment must be disclosed, names TRUNCATED_LOG, and caps any finding drawn from it. The record therefore does not establish that the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 failed; at most it leaves the point open.

The rider knew the driver was there and did not come out. The platform pushed 'Your driver has arrived' to her at 11:11:54, and the single chat entry the impaired log does hold (TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6) is her own message at 11:06:00 saying she was at the Blk 19 lobby and would come out when he reached. She had still not appeared and had not answered the 20 s call when the free wait expired at 11:16:50. The 5.00 SGD is compensation for the driver's time and fuel under POL-NS-22, and on those facts it was earned.

POL-NS-24 has no application here. That clause lets the rider cancel at no charge where the driver missed the pickup by the scheduled time plus 5 minutes, with a goodwill credit if contact was also not attempted. The record carries no scheduled pickup time at all, the driver did arrive and did wait, and the rider never cancelled — the trip was cancelled by the driver for rider no-show. The deadline POL-NS-24 needs is only needed if the rider cancelled, and she did not, so the rider's free-cancellation route is closed and no goodwill credit is owed.

If the panel treats the message limb as unestablished rather than met, POL-GEN-26 governs and still does not give the rider the money. 'Whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling' is one of the facts POL-GEN-26 names by name, and the remedy it prescribes is escalation with the amount held rather than returned. ESCALATE is therefore the correct floor for the driver on this record: the 5.00 SGD stays held pending human review instead of being confirmed back to the rider.
